BUG REPORT (verbatim from user):
"I was adding 61 days to 0099-12-31 and expected to land on 0100-03-02, but the result was 0100-03-01. This happens when the addition crosses the year 100 boundary and goes through February.

```js
const d = DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({ day: 61 });
d.toISODate(); // "0100-03-01", but I expected "0100-03-02"
```"

Your job: find the root cause in /luxon/src (look at leap-year / days-in-month / gregorian calendar helpers, likely src/impl/util.js, src/impl/conversions.js, src/datetime.js) and fix it minimally so that day arithmetic across the year-100 boundary is correct. Note that in the proleptic Gregorian calendar year 100 is NOT a leap year (divisible by 100 but not 400), so 0099-12-31 + 61 days must be 0100-03-02. Check whether the bug is in isLeapYear/daysInMonth or in how the year is computed (e.g. off-by-one/century handling) and make sure years 0-99 and negative years still behave correctly.

IMPORTANT: before changing anything, run the relevant existing test files (e.g. `cd /luxon && npx jest test/datetime test/impl`) and record which tests already fail (baseline). After your fix, no pre-existing passing test may fail. Verify with a small node/babel-node script (e.g. `cd /luxon && npx babel-node -e '...'`) covering the reported case and neighbouring cases (year 99/100/101/199/200/400/1900/2000 boundaries).

Report back: the root cause, the exact file+lines changed, the diff, the verification commands and their results (baseline failures vs after-fix results).

BUG REPORT (verbatim from user):
"I turned on `Settings.throwOnInvalid = true` in my app so that malformed dates blow up loudly instead of silently producing invalid values, and I parse intervals with `Interval.fromISO`. When I pass an interval that combines a date with a duration, it throws instead of returning the interval:

```js
Settings.throwOnInvalid = true;
Interval.fromISO("2020-06-22T17:30:00.000+02:00/PT5H30M");
```

I expected a valid interval back, the same one I get when `throwOnInvalid` is left at its default, but instead I get `InvalidArgumentError: Invalid DateTime`. The same thing happens with the duration first (`"PT5H30M/2020-06-22T17:30:00.000+02:00"`), even though both halves of the string are valid and parse fine on their own."

Your job: find the root cause in /luxon/src (start with src/interval.js `fromISO`, and how DateTime/Duration parsing interacts with Settings.throwOnInvalid in src/settings.js and src/datetime.js), fix it minimally so that Interval.fromISO with a date+duration combination returns the correct valid Interval when Settings.throwOnInvalid is true (and behaves identically to the default-throwOnInvalid case), and verify with a small node/babel-node script plus the existing jest test suites for interval, datetime and duration.

IMPORTANT: before changing anything, run the relevant existing test files (e.g. `cd /luxon && npx jest test/interval test/datetime test/duration`) and record which tests already fail (baseline). After your fix, no pre-existing passing test may fail. Note: tests may need `npx jest` from /luxon; jest config is /luxon/jest.config.js.

Report back: the root cause, the exact file+lines changed, the diff, the verification commands and their results (baseline failures vs after-fix results).

BUG REPORT (verbatim from user):
"I built a fixed-offset zone from a value that isn't a number, and Luxon accepted it as a perfectly good zone instead of rejecting it. I'd expect the zone to report itself as invalid, and any DateTime I create with it to be invalid too, but instead I get a valid DateTime and no error, so the bad offset just silently disappears.

```js
const { DateTime, FixedOffsetZone } = require("luxon");

const zone = new FixedOffsetZone("CDT");
console.log(zone.isValid); // true, but I expected false

const dt = DateTime.fromMillis(0, { zone });
console.log(dt.isValid, dt.invalidReason); // true undefined, but I expected false "unsupported zone"
```"

Your job: find the root cause in /luxon/src (src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js — constructor, offset(), isValid; and how DateTime validates a zone, see src/datetime.js `DateTime.invalid`/`unsupportedZone` and src/zones/zone.js `isValid`, plus `normalizeZone` in src/impl/zoneUtil.js or src/zone.js). Expected: a FixedOffsetZone constructed with a non-numeric offset must report isValid === false, and a DateTime created with such a zone must be invalid with invalidReason 'unsupported zone'. Fix it minimally, without breaking valid fixed-offset zones (e.g. new FixedOffsetZone(360), FixedOffsetZone.utcInstance, FixedOffsetZone.instance(360), 'UTC+3' parsing, and IANA zone handling).

IMPORTANT: before changing anything, run the relevant existing tests (e.g. `cd /luxon && npx jest test/zones test/datetime test/info`) and record the baseline (which tests already fail). After your fix, no pre-existing passing test may fail. Known pre-existing unrelated failures in this container: 2 tests in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js (French locale hour formatting, ICU/CLDR version) — leave them.

Report back: the root cause, the exact file+lines changed, the diff, verification commands and results (baseline vs after-fix), including the reported example and the valid-zone control cases.

You are in charge of final cleanup and verification in the Luxon repository at /luxon. Several concurrent agents have fixed bugs in /luxon/src. Your job:

1. Clean up stray scratch files created by those agents in the repo working tree: run `cd /luxon && git status --short` and delete any UNTRACKED scratch/repro files at the repo root or in src (e.g. repro.js, tmp_repro.js, scratch-repro.js, repro-*.js, *.tmp). Do NOT delete anything tracked by git, do NOT touch node_modules, build/, or test/ files. Report exactly what you deleted.
2. Verify the final state of the repo: run `cd /luxon && git status --short` and `git diff` (summary only, plus full diff of src/ files) and report the complete list of modified source files with their diffs.
3. Run the full test suite: `cd /luxon && npx jest 2>&1 | tail -40`. Report the exact pass/fail counts and the names of any failing tests. Known pre-existing failures (present before any fix): 2 tests in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js about French locale hour formatting ('FFF'/'FFFF', expected "09:23:54" got "9:23:54") due to the container's ICU/CLDR version. Any OTHER failing test is a problem — report it loudly.
4. Run `cd /luxon && npx eslint --quiet src` and report any errors.
5. Verify each of these reported bugs is fixed by running a small script with `cd /luxon && npx babel-node -e '...'` (or a temp file in /tmp, not in the repo):
   a. `Settings.throwOnInvalid = true; Interval.fromISO("2020-06-22T17:30:00.000+02:00/PT5H30M").isValid` must be true and not throw; also `Interval.fromISO("PT5H30M/2020-06-22T17:30:00.000+02:00")` must not throw; then reset Settings.throwOnInvalid = false.
   b. `DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({day:61}).toISODate()` === "0100-03-02".
   c. `DateTime.fromISO("1974-01-07", {zone:"America/Los_Angeles"}).isInDST` === true and `DateTime.fromISO("1974-01-05", {zone:"America/Los_Angeles"}).isInDST` === false, and `DateTime.fromISO("2020-07-15", {zone:"America/Los_Angeles"}).isInDST` === true.
   d. `Duration.fromObject({years:1, quarters:2}).normalize().toObject()` and `Duration.fromObject({quarters:1, seconds:2}).normalize().toObject()` must contain no NaN values.
   e. `DateTime.fromObject({year:-1, month:1, day:1, zone:"utc"}).toISODate()` === "-0001-01-01" and year -10 → "-0010-01-01".
   f. `new FixedOffsetZone("CDT").isValid` === false and `DateTime.fromMillis(0, {zone: new FixedOffsetZone("CDT")}).isValid` === false with invalidReason "unsupported zone"; `new FixedOffsetZone(360).isValid` === true.

Report back a concise summary: files deleted, modified source files + diff summary, full test results, eslint result, and the pass/fail of each of a–f. If any check fails, say so clearly and do not attempt to fix it yourself.
